phase7.title: Kapur Dolomit Rp185.000/kg vs WB BM Rp760/kg
phase7.evidence: WB BM Upah Bahan row 412: Kapur Dolomit Kg Rp760. Canonical raw lines (items 5.4.(2a)/(2b)/(4b)) say 760,00. M40 Kapur M3 Rp185.000 (WB BM row 679) is the misattributed price. Mechanism proven end-to-end: the BM master INPUT JSON (~/workspace/user/files/MASTER_AHSP_BINA_MARGA_2026_AUDITED__1.json, I.256 component_no 5229) carries M40 "M272 kg Kapur Dolomit" kg @185.000 (M40 per-m3 price on a kg unit, polluted name) — the generator faithfully reproduced it into binaMarga2026Master.generated.ts, the adapter emits it, and the audit bound it to M293|kg by name containment. M293 itself appears NOWHERE in the input JSON (0 occurrences). Runtime M293|kg query returns NOT_FOUND (resolver does not reproduce the containment match); hazard dormant except I.256 baked total.
phase7.lawfulFixPath: (a) Input-JSON correction + regeneration: the BM master input JSON EXISTS at ~/workspace/user/files/MASTER_AHSP_BINA_MARGA_2026_AUDITED__1.json (1,137 items, 6,835 components, from PDF 5.-Lampiran-V-Bidang-Bina-Marga-ok.pdf, 3,125 pp) and ALREADY carries the polluted row (I.256 component_no 5229: M40 "M272 kg Kapur Dolomit" kg @185.000, flagged EXTRACTED_FROM_SUMMARY_NEEDS_LINE_BY_LINE_PDF_VERIFICATION) — so re-extraction alone would reproduce the error; the input row must be corrected first (owner approval — it is the owner's file), and the generator script (JSON -> .generated.ts) is MISSING from the repo (no script references the JSON). (b) Adapter overlay (practical path): binaMarga2026Adapter.ts is hand-written (not generated) — a correction map there is lawful (same pattern as ahspDescriptionCorrections.ts): drop/rename the polluted M40 "M272 kg Kapur Dolomit" entry + add M293 @760/kg with provenance WB BM row 412. (c) Registry overlay for item I.256 baked component (mapBinaMargaToNational). (d) Owner approval required before applying (a)/(b)/(c) — NOT applied in §5. Golden pre-check: no golden fixture references M293 items (5.4.*) or I.256/I.257 by code.
